title: Brake Service Warranties: One Warranty per Brake Job and Axle
content:
**The rule.** A customer may hold any number of Brake Service Warranties — there is no maximum per customer. Each brake job on each axle of each vehicle opens its own warranty, with its own dates, odometer and replacement history. Warranties never share replacements or noise services. How many warranties one axle may carry is governed by the separate limit on active warranties per axle.

**The same rule, unit by unit.**

| Unit | What it has of its own |
|---|---|
| One brake job | its own warranty |
| One axle of that job (front or rear) | its own warranty, dates and odometer |
| One vehicle | its own warranties, one opened per job per axle |
| One warranty | its own replacement history and its own noise services |
| One customer | any number of warranties, with no maximum |

**Training questions answered.**

*A customer had brake jobs done on both the front and the rear axle of one vehicle. How many warranties is that?* Two. Each axle's job opens its own warranty, each with its own dates, odometer and replacement history.

*Can a replacement made under one warranty be counted against another warranty of the same customer?* No. Warranties never share replacements, so each warranty's replacement history counts only the replacements made under it.

*Do noise services pool across a customer's warranties?* No. Warranties never share noise services; each warranty counts its own.

*Is there a ceiling on how many brake warranties one customer may hold?* No. A customer may hold any number.

**Illustration (hypothetical household).** A household with two vehicles has a front brake job on each vehicle and a rear brake job on one of them. That is three brake jobs on three axles, so three warranties, each with its own dates, odometer, replacement history and noise services.
